upstream.relationship: Primary foundry for all NVIDIA GPU and SoC fabrication (3nm, 4nm, 5nm nodes)

upstream.name: ASML Holding
upstream.relationship: Sole supplier of EUV lithography equipment to TSMC used in NVIDIA chip production; indirect but existential dependency

upstream.name: Applied Materials
upstream.relationship: Semiconductor fabrication equipment and materials supplier supporting NVIDIA's manufacturing partners

upstream.name: Marvell Technology
upstream.relationship: Custom networking ASICs and high-speed interconnect components used in NVIDIA DGX/HGX systems

upstream.name: Micron Technology
upstream.relationship: High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and GDDR6X DRAM supplier critical for GPU memory stacks

upstream.name: Broadcom Inc.
upstream.relationship: Custom networking silicon, PCIe switches, and NVLink fabric components; also co-develops custom AI accelerators competing and complementing NVIDIA

downstream.name: Microsoft Corporation
downstream.relationship: Largest hyperscaler customer; procures H100/H200/GB200 GPUs at massive scale for Azure AI cloud services and OpenAI partnership

downstream.name: Meta Platforms
downstream.relationship: Major data center GPU customer; has publicly committed to purchasing ~600,000 H100 GPUs for AI/Llama model training

downstream.name: Alphabet Inc.
downstream.relationship: Significant hyperscaler customer for data center GPUs across Google Cloud and internal AI research (DeepMind); also competes with own TPUs

downstream.name: Amazon.com Inc.
downstream.relationship: Major AWS cloud GPU customer deploying H100/A100 clusters for cloud AI services; also competes via Trainium/Inferentia chips

downstream.name: Tesla Inc.
downstream.relationship: Customer for automotive-grade GPUs (Drive platform) and historically large buyer of A100 GPUs for Dojo supercomputer training

downstream.name: Dell Technologies
downstream.relationship: Key OEM system integrator; sells NVIDIA GPU-powered AI servers (PowerEdge XE9680) to enterprise customers, acting as a major distribution channel

NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI compute value chain as a fabless semiconductor designer, critically dependent on TSMC for cutting-edge chip fabrication and on HBM suppliers like Micron and SK Hynix for GPU memory, while its downstream is dominated by hyperscalers (Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta) racing to build AI infrastructure at scale. Its near-monopoly position in AI accelerators (>80% market share in data center GPUs) gives it extraordinary pricing power with customers, though its single-foundry dependency on TSMC represents its most significant supply chain concentration risk.

upstream.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.
upstream.relationship: Primary fab for Apple Silicon (A-series, M-series, S-series chips) on leading-edge nodes

upstream.name: Qualcomm Inc.
upstream.relationship: Supplier of 5G modem chipsets used in iPhone models (transitioning to in-house modem)

upstream.name: Broadcom Inc.
upstream.relationship: Supplier of Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and RF networking chips across iPhone, iPad, and Mac

upstream.name: Honeywell International
upstream.relationship: Supplier of specialty materials and sensors used in device manufacturing and industrial components

upstream.name: Applied Materials Inc.
upstream.relationship: Semiconductor process equipment supplier to TSMC and Samsung fabs that produce Apple chips (indirect critical dependency)

downstream.name: Verizon Communications
downstream.relationship: Major U.S. carrier distributing and subsidizing iPhone through wireless service bundles

downstream.name: AT&T Inc.
downstream.relationship: Major U.S. carrier distributing iPhone; partnership for carrier activation and installment plans

downstream.name: T-Mobile US
downstream.relationship: Major U.S. carrier distributing iPhone with exclusive promotions and device financing

downstream.name: Alphabet Inc.
downstream.relationship: Pays Apple estimated $15-20B annually as default search engine on Safari (Services revenue contributor)

downstream.name: Amazon.com Inc.
downstream.relationship: Retail distribution partner selling Apple hardware; also an App Store developer generating commission revenue

downstream.name: Meta Platforms Inc.
downstream.relationship: Major App Store developer and advertiser; pays Apple 30% commission on in-app purchases across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp apps

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly complex global supply chain, acting primarily as a design-and-brand house that outsources manufacturing to contract assemblers (notably Foxconn/Hon Hai) and chip fabrication to TSMC, while selling its integrated hardware-software ecosystem through carriers, retail partners, and its own stores worldwide. Its downstream relationships are increasingly defined by Services revenue — including App Store commissions, search licensing deals (Google TAC), and subscription platforms — making Apple both a hardware supplier and a platform gatekeeper to millions of third-party developers and enterprise customers.

upstream.name: ASML Holding N.V.
upstream.relationship: Primary supplier of EUV and DUV lithography equipment critical for advanced DRAM and NAND manufacturing

upstream.name: Applied Materials Inc.
upstream.relationship: Major supplier of deposition, etch, and CMP equipment for memory fab operations

upstream.name: Lam Research Corporation
upstream.relationship: Key supplier of etch and deposition equipment essential for 3D NAND stacking and DRAM patterning

upstream.name: KLA Corporation
upstream.relationship: Supplier of process control, inspection, and metrology equipment for yield management in memory fabs

upstream.name: Sherwin-Williams / Element Solutions
upstream.relationship: Supplier of specialty chemicals, photoresists, and CMP slurries for semiconductor manufacturing processes

upstream.name: CMC Materials (Entegris/CMC)
upstream.relationship: Supplier of CMP slurries, polishing pads, and ultra-high purity process materials for memory chip fabrication

downstream.name: Amazon.com Inc.
downstream.relationship: Major hyperscale cloud customer purchasing DRAM, HBM, and NAND for AWS data center infrastructure

downstream.name: Microsoft Corporation
downstream.relationship: Large cloud and enterprise customer buying server DRAM and SSD storage for Azure and enterprise platforms

downstream.name: NVIDIA Corporation
downstream.relationship: Critical customer for HBM3/HBM3E memory integrated into AI GPU accelerators (H100, H200, Blackwell); fastest-growing segment

downstream.name: Apple Inc.
downstream.relationship: Significant customer for LPDDR mobile DRAM and NAND flash used in iPhone, iPad, and Mac product lines

downstream.name: Alphabet Inc.
downstream.relationship: Hyperscale customer purchasing server DRAM, SSDs, and HBM for Google Cloud and internal AI infrastructure

downstream.name: Dell Technologies Inc.
downstream.relationship: OEM customer incorporating Micron DRAM modules and SSDs into servers, PCs, and enterprise storage solutions

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits at the heart of the global memory supply chain, converting highly specialized semiconductor manufacturing equipment and process chemicals from a concentrated set of equipment suppliers into DRAM, NAND, and HBM products sold to hyperscalers, AI compute leaders, and consumer electronics OEMs. Its upstream is capital-intensive and dominated by a handful of equipment makers (ASML, AMAT, LRCX), while its downstream is increasingly driven by AI infrastructure demand—particularly HBM for NVIDIA GPUs—alongside traditional cloud, mobile, and PC markets.

upstream.name: Cadence Design Systems
upstream.relationship: EDA tools supplier for IP design and verification workflows

upstream.name: Synopsys Inc.
upstream.relationship: EDA tools and IP verification software supplier critical to chip design

upstream.name: Microsoft Corporation
upstream.relationship: Cloud infrastructure and enterprise software provider for R&D operations

upstream.name: Alphabet Inc.
upstream.relationship: Cloud computing infrastructure provider supporting design and simulation workloads

upstream.name: Applied Materials
upstream.relationship: Indirect upstream dependency via process technology research informing ARM IP design rules

downstream.name: Qualcomm Inc.
downstream.relationship: Major architecture licensee; uses ARM CPU IP in Snapdragon mobile and automotive SoCs

downstream.name: Apple Inc.
downstream.relationship: Architecture licensee and largest royalty contributor via iPhone/Mac chips (A-series, M-series)

downstream.name: NVIDIA Corporation
downstream.relationship: Architecture and technology licensee; uses ARM IP in Grace CPU and Tegra/Drive platforms

downstream.name: Microsoft Corporation
downstream.relationship: Licensee deploying ARM-based CPUs in Azure cloud infrastructure and Surface devices

downstream.name: Amazon.com Inc.

downstream.name: MediaTek Inc.
downstream.relationship: High-volume ARM licensee using ARM CPU/GPU IP across mobile, IoT, and smart TV chipsets

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM Holdings occupies a uniquely capital-light position at the apex of the semiconductor IP ecosystem, licensing CPU, GPU, and system IP to virtually every major chip designer rather than manufacturing silicon itself. Its upstream dependencies are primarily on EDA software vendors like Cadence and Synopsys, while its downstream relationships span the breadth of the global semiconductor industry — from mobile SoC leaders like Apple and Qualcomm to hyperscale cloud providers building custom silicon, making ARM a foundational but non-exclusive chokepoint in modern computing.

upstream.relationship: EUV lithography equipment supplier to TSMC enabling Marvell's advanced node production

upstream.name: Cadence Design Systems
upstream.relationship: EDA software tools for chip design and verification

upstream.name: Synopsys Inc.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology operates as a fabless semiconductor company, sitting between upstream foundry and EDA toolchain partners—critically dependent on TSMC for advanced-node manufacturing—and a diverse downstream customer base spanning hyperscale cloud providers (Amazon, Google, Microsoft) and networking/storage OEMs. The company is increasingly pivoting toward custom AI ASIC co-design for hyperscalers, making its downstream relationships with cloud giants increasingly strategic and revenue-concentrated.
